ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image shows a cube (die) with an octahedron inside it, and the octahedron's six vertices are located at the centers of the cube's six faces. Model the cube of side length 1 with its center at the origin. Then the six face centers are at (±1/2, 0, 0), (0, ±1/2, 0), and (0, 0, ±1/2). These are exactly the vertices of the octahedron. The octahedron can be divided into 8 congruent tetrahedra, one in each octant. In one octant, the tetrahedron has intercepts 1/2 on the x-, y-, and z-axes, so its volume is (1/6)(1/2)(1/2)(1/2) = 1/48. Since there are 8 such tetrahedra, the total volume is 8 · 1/48 = 1/6.
